title: Day-trader mode: wire GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators and GET /api/portfolio/GET /api/portfolio/risk once their prerequisites land
description:
backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api's own PR scoped down to just `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` and `GET /api/watchlist` (+`GET /api/watchlist/breadth`, which shares the same helper) given the number of endpoints in its original checklist and the regression risk on swing mode -- see that task's `decisions` entry for the full scoping rationale. This task tracks the two endpoints it deferred:

- `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators` -- structurally blocked on `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-history` landing first: this endpoint is powered by `app.signals.engine.analyse_history()`'s walk-forward per-bar replay, which has no day-trader-mode support yet (confirmed in docs/architecture/Backend.md's own 'Not yet landed' list at the time this task was filed).
- `GET /api/portfolio` / `GET /api/portfolio/risk` -- `GET /api/portfolio`'s own per-position `signal`/`confidence`/`confidence_band` fields could in principle be wired the same way `GET /api/watchlist` was (via `app.api.day_trader_signal.compute_day_trader_signal`), but `GET /api/portfolio/risk`'s `protective_stop`/`profit_target`/exit-flag fields need `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk`'s own genericization of `app.portfolio.risk`/`app.portfolio.profit_target`/`app.portfolio.exits` first (still hard-coded weekly/daily today, confirmed unaffected by backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api's own PR) -- wiring `GET /api/portfolio`'s signal field alone, ahead of `GET /api/portfolio/risk`, would leave the two portfolio endpoints inconsistently day-trader-aware for the same position, which this task's own checklist should decide whether to do anyway or wait and land both together. `GET /api/portfolio`'s per-position day-trader-mode fetch also means one IBKR round-trip per held position per request -- worth a dedicated latency/design pass (e.g. concurrent per-position fetches, matching `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators`'s existing daily/weekly `ThreadPoolExecutor` pattern) rather than a naive sequential loop, given `app.data.day_trader_intraday`'s own already-noted 'sequential-not-concurrent 3-leg IBKR fetch latency' non-blocking finding (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups.json).

checklist.step: Decide (and record via `decisions`) whether GET /api/portfolio's signal field is wired ahead of GET /api/portfolio/risk landing, or whether both wait for backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk to land together.

Wire GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators to use analyse_history's day-trader-mode support (once backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-history lands) when day-trader mode is active, with swing mode's existing behavior preserved exactly (regression tests).

Wire GET /api/portfolio and GET /api/portfolio/risk to use the generic day-trader-mode signal/risk computation (once backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk lands) per the decision above, with swing mode's existing behavior preserved exactly (regression tests) -- decide whether concurrent per-position IBKR fetches are needed for acceptable latency.
Unit/integration tests for the updated endpoints under both swing and day-trader mode.

Non-blocking finding from backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api's PR #313 review: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis (app/api/routers/stocks.py's get_analysis) always fetches daily_ohlcv/weekly_ohlcv/extended_data from the swing DataProvider -- and maps TickerNotFoundError/InsufficientHistoryError/DataProviderUnavailableError to 404/422/503 -- before checking whether day-trader mode is active, so a ticker IBKR could fully compute a day-trader signal for, but that the swing provider doesn't recognize or has fewer than 26 weeks of weekly history for, gets a 404/422 and never reaches compute_day_trader_signal at all. GET /api/watchlist's day-trader branch has no such dependency (it returns from compute_day_trader_signal before ever touching daily/weekly), so the same ticker+mode combination is handled inconsistently between the two endpoints. Worth resolving as part of this follow-up's own work on these two endpoints (or explicitly deciding it's acceptable given as_of/support_resistance_zones/profit_target/extended_data staying always swing-data-derived regardless of trading mode).

Non-blocking finding from backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api's PR #313 round-2 review (code-review pass): in day-trader mode, GET /api/watchlist and GET /api/watchlist/breadth (app/api/routers/watchlist.py) now perform up to 4 sequential IBKR round-trips (1 conid resolve + 3 leg fetches, via compute_day_trader_signal) per tracked ticker, with no concurrency across tickers -- worse than swing mode's pre-existing 2-round-trips-per-ticker sequential fetch (already flagged generally in backend-watchlist-breadth-proxy-followups.json). A watchlist/portfolio tracking N tickers under day-trader mode with a slow/high-latency IBKR gateway turns GET /api/watchlist/breadth into up to 4N sequential blocking calls in one request handler. Worth a concurrency pass (e.g. per-ticker ThreadPoolExecutor, matching GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators's existing daily/weekly concurrent-fetch pattern) when this follow-up's own portfolio-endpoint latency design pass happens.

Non-blocking finding from backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api's PR #313 round-2 review (code-review pass): tests/integration/test_watchlist.py's new TestDayTraderMode class's _client_with_ibkr helper (via _make_client) sets app.dependency_overrides[get_db]/[get_data_provider] but never pops them in a finally/teardown -- only get_ibkr_provider is cleaned up, via the class's autouse _clear_ibkr_override fixture. This mirrors an existing repo-wide gap in the same file (_client_with_provider, used since before this PR, has the identical never-popped get_db/get_data_provider issue for its own many call sites) rather than a regression introduced here, but TestDayTraderMode is now the file's last class, so after its last test runs, a disposed in-memory SQLite session and a stale _StubProvider are left registered as the process-wide get_db/get_data_provider overrides for any later-collected test elsewhere in the suite that hits a DB-or-provider-backed route via an unguarded TestClient(app) -- a latent, collection-order-dependent flakiness risk worth cleaning up (in this file and, ideally, at _client_with_provider's root cause) rather than leaving to chance.

decisions.decision: GET /api/portfolio's signal field and GET /api/portfolio/risk's protective_stop/trailing_stop/exit_flags/profit_target are wired in the SAME PR (this task), not staggered.
decisions.rationale: The original scoping concern (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api's own decisions entry) was that wiring only GET /api/portfolio's signal field ahead of GET /api/portfolio/risk would leave the two portfolio endpoints inconsistently day-trader-aware for the same position. By the time this task started, backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk (the prerequisite that concern was waiting on) had already landed and merged (PR #317) -- so there was no longer a reason to stagger; landing both together in one PR resolves the original inconsistency concern directly rather than deferring it further.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 7's non-blocking finding (GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis fetching daily/weekly from the swing DataProvider before checking whether day-trader mode is active) is left AS-IS on that endpoint -- explicitly decided acceptable, not fixed by this task. GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators, which this task builds fresh, is instead designed to check the active trading mode FIRST and only touch the swing DataProvider in its swing branch, so the same class of inconsistency doesn't exist for the new endpoint.
decisions.rationale: Fixing /analysis's own fetch order would mean restructuring an already-shipped, already-reviewed endpoint that is explicitly outside this task's own checklist scope (items 2/3 name /indicators and /portfolio/portfolio-risk, not /analysis) -- doing so risks the exact kind of regression this whole feature area's own review history has repeatedly flagged as a real, not hypothetical, concern (see backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine's own decisions entry). The inconsistency itself is also bounded in practice: it only manifests for a ticker IBKR can fully compute a day-trader signal for but that the swing provider doesn't recognize (or has under 26 weeks of weekly history for) -- a narrow edge case, not a routine one. Resolving it for the NEW endpoint (/indicators) by construction, while leaving the existing endpoint's behavior untouched, was judged the better tradeoff than either forcing an unscoped fix onto /analysis or introducing the identical inconsistency into /indicators for consistency's own sake.

decisions.decision: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators's day-trader-mode branch never reads or writes the existing same-calendar-day IndicatorHistoryResponseCache -- every day-trader-mode request is computed fresh. Its `range` query param's existing grammar (`<N>d`/`<N>w`/`<N>m`/`<N>y`/`max`) is also left unextended -- no new minute/hour unit was added for finer-than-a-day trimming of an intraday chart, and a day-trader-mode request always uses `fetch_day_trader_history_legs`'s own default lookback (mirroring `analyse_history`'s swing-mode convention of always fetching a large fixed amount of history and letting `range` only trim what's returned) rather than translating `range` into a smaller explicit `lookback_days` IBKR request.
decisions.rationale: The existing cache's TTL is explicitly calendar-day-grained, sized for swing mode's genuinely once-daily cadence -- serving an hours-old (or wrong-trading-mode) cached response for data that can change every few minutes would be actively wrong, not just stale-by-degree the way swing mode's own cache tradeoff already accepts. Extending the cache schema to be mode/triple-aware with a much shorter intraday-appropriate TTL is a distinct, larger design problem this task's own checklist doesn't ask for, and 'never cache in day-trader mode' already matches the precedent GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis and GET /api/watchlist set for their own day-trader-mode signal computation (always live, no caching layer). On the range grammar: adding a minute/hour unit would need its own validation-pattern change, description updates, and interacts with `_RangeOutOfBoundsError`'s existing bounds-checking -- a real, separable feature addition, not a mechanical wiring task, and no frontend consumer exists yet to need finer-than-a-day trimming of a day-trader-mode chart (no settings UI to reach the mode at all). Verified via a dedicated integration test (test_range_trims_the_computed_points_using_a_calendar_day_window) that day-or-coarser trimming still works correctly for intraday data through the existing grammar.

decisions.decision: IndicatorHistoryResponse.points[].date stays a plain calendar `date` (not widened to a full timestamp) even in day-trader mode, where several consecutive points can legitimately share the same calendar date whenever the active triple's intermediate leg is finer than one day (e.g. several 10-minute bars per day).
decisions.rationale: Widening/renaming this field to carry time-of-day would be a breaking API-schema change for a feature no frontend can reach yet (no day-trader-mode settings UI exists) -- the identical non-breaking-change rationale backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api's own decisions entry already established for not renaming screens.tide/weekly_macd_histogram_slope/etc. The alternative (a distinct day-trader-only response shape with a real timestamp field) was considered and rejected as unwarranted scope growth for the same reason. This is a real, accepted limitation, not a hidden one -- test_fully_intraday_triple_replays_a_real_walk_forward_history explicitly asserts the resulting date-collapse behavior (27 points, 1 distinct date) rather than leaving it unverified, so a future task revisiting this (once a real frontend consumer exists) has a concrete test to update deliberately.

decisions.decision: The per-position IBKR-fetch latency concern (GET /api/portfolio's per-position signal, GET /api/portfolio/risk's per-position legs) is resolved via a new per-ticker concurrent fan-out (`app.api.day_trader_signal.compute_day_trader_signals_concurrently`/`fetch_day_trader_legs_concurrently`, a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor of at most 8 concurrent tickers) rather than raising IBKRProvider's own internal pagination/concurrency bounds or adding an async request-batching layer. GET /api/watchlist/GET /api/watchlist/breadth (checklist item 8's own finding) are wired to the same fan-out helper, resolving that finding too, in the same PR.
decisions.rationale: Each ticker's own three-leg fetch was already concurrent within itself (`app.data.day_trader_intraday._fetch_legs_concurrently`, landed by an earlier task in this chain) -- the remaining latency problem was purely across TICKERS (a watchlist/portfolio of N tickers still paying N sequential per-ticker round trips), which a second, ticker-level thread pool addresses directly with no change to the already-reviewed per-leg fetch mechanics. A worker cap of 8 (not unbounded, not a smaller/larger number, not a configurable setting) was chosen as a reasonable round default: `IBKRProvider`'s Client Portal gateway is a single local process, so concurrency past a point contends for the same gateway rather than shortening wall-clock latency further, and this app has no evidence yet (no live gateway available in any sandboxed/CI environment, per `app.data.ibkr_provider`'s own documented testing constraint) that a different number would meaningfully change real-world behavior -- matching this codebase's existing precedent of picking small, fixed constants for internal concurrency knobs rather than exposing a tuning parameter nothing yet needs. GET /api/portfolio/risk's fan-out (`fetch_day_trader_legs_concurrently`) reuses the exact same full three-leg fetch `compute_day_trader_signal` uses (fetching `short_term_ohlcv` even though none of protective_stop/suggest_profit_target/evaluate_exit_flags read it) rather than building a second, leaner two-leg-only fetch pipeline -- the unused leg is still fetched *concurrently* alongside the two needed ones (no added sequential cost), and one shared, already-tested degrade-gracefully/concurrency code path was judged a better tradeoff than a second bespoke pipeline solely to shave one already-parallel IBKR call. See app/api/day_trader_signal.py's own module docstring ("Per-ticker concurrency") and DayTraderLegsOutcome's docstring for the same rationale recorded in code.

decisions.decision: Fixed a genuine bug this task's own integration testing surfaced in `app.portfolio.risk.ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`: comparing a tz-AWARE `DatetimeIndex` (day-trader-mode's IBKR-sourced OHLCV, which carries real UTC timestamps) against a tz-naive `pd.Timestamp(position.entry_date)` raised `TypeError`, not caught by that function's existing `isinstance(daily_ohlcv.index, pd.DatetimeIndex)` guard (which only handled a non-`DatetimeIndex` fallback, e.g. a plain `RangeIndex`). Fixed by localizing the naive `entry_cutoff` to the index's own tz (`.tz_localize(daily_ohlcv.index.tz)`) when the index is tz-aware, rather than converting `daily_ohlcv.index` to naive or stripping tz info from the IBKR-sourced frame upstream.
decisions.rationale: Localizing (not converting) is correct because `position.entry_date` is a plain calendar `date` with no tz concept of its own in either trading mode -- it represents 'this calendar date,' and localizing it to the index's own tz at midnight is the natural reading, matching what a naive comparison already does implicitly for swing mode's own naive index. Stripping tz info from the IBKR-sourced frame instead (upstream, in app.data.day_trader_intraday) was considered and rejected: IBKR's real UTC timestamps are meaningful, correct data this app should keep, not discard to work around a comparison bug one layer up -- the bug belongs to (and is fixed in) the comparison, not the data. This was unreachable by any existing swing-mode caller (yfinance/Stooq's own index is always naive), which is why no prior review pass of this already-reviewed function (backend-trailing-profit-stop, backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk) ever caught it -- found here specifically because this task is the first to exercise ratchet_trailing_profit_stop through GET /api/portfolio/risk with a real tz-aware IBKR-shaped fixture end to end. Verified via mutation testing (temporarily disabled the tz-localize branch, confirmed both the new unit test and the new integration test fail with the original TypeError, then restored and reran clean).

decisions.decision: Checklist item 9's test-teardown fix (tests/integration/test_watchlist.py's TestDayTraderMode never popping get_db/get_data_provider overrides) is scoped narrowly to that one class's own autouse fixture (renamed `_clear_ibkr_override` -> `_clear_overrides`, now also popping get_db/get_data_provider) -- the same pre-existing gap in `_client_with_provider`'s own many call sites elsewhere in that file (used since before this PR, per the finding's own text) is NOT also fixed here.
decisions.rationale: The finding's own text already frames `_client_with_provider`'s gap as a distinct, pre-existing, repo-wide pattern predating this feature area entirely, not something introduced by (or in scope for) this task's own day-trader-mode work -- fixing it properly would mean auditing/updating every one of that helper's many call sites across this file, a larger, separable cleanup this task's checklist item doesn't itself call for. The narrower fix directly closes the concrete, immediate risk the finding flagged (TestDayTraderMode being the file's LAST class, so its leaked overrides could affect any later-collected test in the suite) without taking on unrelated scope creep.

comments.summary: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators's same-calendar-day response cache can serve a stale `trading_mode` field after the global trading mode changes between requests -- a cached IndicatorHistoryResponse's trading_mode is baked in at write time and returned as-is on a cache hit, never refreshed to the freshly-resolved current setting. Narrow in practice (only reachable while the swing branch is still being taken with a cache hit) but undocumented as an accepted tradeoff. Non-blocking; tracked on backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups-followups.

GET /api/portfolio/risk's first-pass loop duplicates ~15 lines of near-identical logic (drop_malformed_daily_bars/length-check/protective_stop try-except) across the day_trader_active and swing branches, differing only in where daily_ohlcv/weekly_ohlcv come from -- a maintenance hazard, not a bug. Non-blocking; tracked on backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups-followups.

position_risk_pct's 'distance to stop' in day-trader mode mixes a swing-derived current_price (EOD daily close) with a day-trader-mode-derived protective_stop (IBKR intraday-leg-based) for the same position -- the 2%-rule risk percentage spans two different data sources/timeframes. Follows the already-reviewed PR #317 generalization precedent (not introduced fresh here), but this PR makes it reachable end-to-end via the real endpoint with no decisions entry addressing the interaction. Non-blocking; tracked on backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups-followups.

test_portfolio_get.py's TestDayTraderMode class only exercises single-position scenarios -- the discriminating 'does the concurrent fan-out mix up which ticker gets which outcome' test exists at the unit level (test_day_trader_signal.py) but not as a GET /api/portfolio integration test with 2+ positions. Non-blocking; tracked on backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups-followups.

review.notes: Full review: independently re-ran backend (pytest --cov=app, 1398 passed, 100% coverage), frontend (yarn test:coverage, 882 passed, 99%+), ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc (all clean), scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py and scripts/validate_tasks.py (clean). Regenerated backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts myself -- zero diff against committed snapshots, confirming genuine sync. Ran the full persisted e2e Playwright suite (make e2e) against a fresh stack -- 26/26 specs passed. No Playwright MCP browser tool was available in this session, so substituted a manual API-level (curl) golden-path + edge-case walkthrough of every touched endpoint in both swing and day-trader (IBKR-disabled) mode against a live make dev stack -- all responses matched documented behavior exactly. Mutation-tested all three claims flagged for extra scrutiny: (1) reproduced the pre-fix TypeError directly and confirmed the tz-localize fix in ratchet_trailing_profit_stop is semantically correct (unit test asserts tz-aware result equals naive-equivalent exactly, not just non-crashing); (2) disabled the day-trader-mode dispatch in get_indicator_history and confirmed all 7 TestDayTraderMode tests genuinely fail (proving mode-check-before-swing-DataProvider ordering); (3) made _fan_out_per_ticker return the last-completed future's result for every ticker key and confirmed the swap-detection unit tests genuinely fail. Ran code-review (found the two non-blocking findings above plus confirmed no other correctness bugs), verify-elder-signal (no methodology drift -- app.portfolio.risk/profit_target/exits logic itself unchanged, only the tz fix touches risk.py), and architecture-review (module placement, API doc standard, no new dependency/layer all conform) checklists explicitly. Cross-checked the one 'decide X' checklist item against the decisions array -- present and adequately reasoned. Spot-checked several of the ~12 updated frontend fixture files -- all mechanical (adding the required trading_mode field) plus incidental prettier reformatting of unrelated nearby lines, no assertion/behavior changes.
